description: Spec-derived recommendation judgments over tests/fixtures/demo/research_site.jsonl (Phase 3, ADR-0011). Written from the ADR, the fixture taxonomy, relatedness.json and the corpus text BEFORE the engine existed; never paste engine output in here.

conventions.urls: Canonical page URLs, as the export declares them.
conventions.good: Should be recommended: a strong relation (relatedness.json rubric) AND an unlinked natural mention in an eligible block (p/li, no existing link). 'mention' cites the phrase expected as anchor; 'relationship' is the expected RelationshipType from the source's view (informational, not gated).
conventions.acceptable: Fine but not required: weak relations, cross-geography same-topic links, or strong relations without a free mention.
conventions.bad: Must never be recommended for this source. kind: geography_only | shared_word | intent_mismatch | unrelated_market | topic_mismatch | ineligible.
conventions.unjudged: A plan to a target not listed for its source is UNJUDGED: it counts as not relevant in precision and is reported separately.

rules.R1: Every relatedness.json 'unrelated' pair involving the source is BAD unless listed explicitly.
rules.R2: Listing hubs (/, /industry-reports, /insights) and the market-less digest /insights/q3-market-update are BAD targets for every source (intent mismatch).
rules.R3: An industry hub (/industries/<id>) is ACCEPTABLE for sources of that industry and BAD otherwise.
rules.R4: Every page that analysis_expected.json marks not linkable as a target is BAD (and a must-not).

metrics.precision_at_3: Per judged source with >= 1 plan: |plans in GOOD or ACCEPTABLE| / |plans| (plans <= max_plans_per_source = 3). Macro mean over those sources; micro also reported.
metrics.recall_good: Per judged source with GOOD: |plans in GOOD| / min(|GOOD|, max_plans_per_source). Macro mean.
metrics.bad_rate: Plans from judged sources whose target is BAD / all plans from judged sources.
metrics.anchor_exact_match: Over the expected_anchors pairs that the engine proposed: share whose anchor_text equals the expected anchor exactly (verbatim, case-sensitive).

must_not.description: Hard gates over ALL plans of a run (zero tolerance).

rules.rule: No plan whose source is not linkable as a source (hubs, corporate/legal/contact, protected, draft, thin or mid-length, canonical alias).
No plan whose target is not linkable as a target (corporate/legal/contact, protected, draft, thin, canonical alias).
No plan whose source or target has an active protection (DB page_protections).
No plan whose source or target page is gone.
No self-link (by page id and canonical URL).
No plan to a target the source's CURRENT version already links to (resolved through known_urls: aliases and redirects count).
The anchor is never a geography label or alias on its own.
The anchor is never one of placement.forbidden_anchors; word and character limits hold.
The anchor block kind is in placement.block_kinds (p, li); never a heading.
The anchor span never sits under an excluded ancestor (a, table, blockquote, figure, figcaption, pre, code, cite, q, sup, sub, h1-h6, caption). Exercised by the placement_safety pages below.
The anchor never overlaps an existing link, and a block never exceeds max_links_per_block counting existing and planned links.
anchor_text == block_text[start:end] and context_hash == sha256(block_text) of the source version.
At most selection.max_plans_per_source plans per source per run.
At most selection.max_plans_per_target_per_run plans per target per run.
(existing internal body links + plans + 0) / words x 100 <= max_internal_links_per_100_words.
Never two open plans for the same (source, target).
Never two open plans for the same (source, context_hash, start), and no overlapping spans within a source.
relevance >= min_relevance and total >= min_score; total == relevance x placement_quality.
calibration_version is null and confidence == total (raw, never presented as calibrated).

placement_safety.description: One synthetic, eligible report appended to the corpus by the integration eval (never written into research_site.jsonl). Every market phrase on it sits under an excluded ancestor (heading, table caption/th, p inside td, p inside blockquote, p inside figure, figcaption, pre/code, cite, q, code, sup, sub), inside a block that already holds a link, or is a bare geography; only the two control paragraphs may host a plan.

record.title: India Electric Vehicle Placement Safety Report
record.meta_description: Synthetic placement-safety fixture for the Phase 3 recommendation evals.
record.body_html:
India Electric Vehicle Placement Safety Report

This synthetic page exists only to test placement safety. It mixes protected markup with ordinary paragraphs. Every market phrase on the page sits inside markup where no new anchor may ever be placed, except in the two control paragraphs near the end.

Charging infrastructure and battery storage for electric vehicles

Rooftop solar capacity
Cold chain

Auto parts suppliers

Battery storage and rooftop solar will decide grid stability, one operator told us.

cold chain, data centers

Survey responses were drawn from The Cold Chain Review and the battery storage index, with notes kept in rooftop solar and footnotes data center auto parts.

Lenders say auto parts suppliers want working capital, and charging infrastructure is still thin outside the largest cities.

Buyers in India want lower prices, and Indian lenders remain cautious about resale values.

Electric vehicle demand outlook

Across the country, charging infrastructure is expanding along highways, which helps fleet operators plan longer routes and gives buyers more confidence about range.

Most packs are still assembled from imported lithium-ion battery cells, so margins depend on exchange rates and on the price of cathode inputs.

The remaining notes summarise interviews with dealers, fleet owners and lenders in twelve cities. Respondents were asked about prices, financing, resale values and the service network, and their answers were weighted by city size before being combined into the indicators reported here.
